subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should OpenClaw preserve `reason: "target-none"` as the machine-readable heartbeat skip contract and add a human-readable disabled-delivery hint, or rename the reason itself?
rationale: Both viable fixes affect exposed diagnostics: a rename is simpler for humans but changes a parsed value, while an additive hint keeps compatibility but expands the event/status contract.

options.title: Add additive hint
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a disabled-delivery hint or equivalent display field, and update CLI/status formatting plus tests.

options.title: Rename the reason
options.body: Change the machine reason to a clearer value such as `delivery-disabled`, accepting the compatibility cost for private parsers or scripts.

options.title: Leave current output
options.body: Keep the raw `target-none` wording and rely on docs, accepting the existing operator confusion as low-priority UX friction.

recommendation.title: Add additive hint
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a disabled-delivery hint or equivalent display field, and update CLI/status formatting plus tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the default-none behavior and have the clearest product context for whether this exposed diagnostic should stay compatible or be renamed.
